defClientAuth: clientAuth is none, optional (the default) or required — a listener for mutual TLS.
defFiles: Without certificate files the {whose, select, default {default realm's} other {realm's}} certificate authority issues one for hostnames.
defTls: tls takes the per-listener TLS settings by their short names (disableTls12, tls13CipherSuites, pqcOnly, ...).
defAnswers: {whose, select, default {These answer every realm.} other {These answer this realm alone.}} Empty for none.
headWhichOn: Which application is on which listener
mapObject: A JSON object from an application id, or * for every one not named, to
mapMain: main is the main port. An application not named is on main alone.
mapRealmFirst: This realm's entries are read before the service's, which are
mapIssuer: Changing where oauth-oidc is advertised changes the issuer every token and client names. Taking management-api off the listener this page was reached on needs the confirmation below; STS_LISTENERS_ADMIN_ON_MAIN=true puts the console and the API back on the main port at the next start.
confirmOff: Take the management API off the listener this page was reached on, if this does
rescueText: listeners.adminOnMain is on: the console and the management API are on the main port and advertised there, whatever the mapping says.
builtInDefault: The built-in listeners, which every realm is served on.
builtInRealm: The built-in listeners. Their settings are the service's and are changed in the default realm; this realm is served on them under its /realm/{realm} prefix, and on its own listeners where its mapping says.
clientCertBefore: "Client certificate" is none (no CertificateRequest), optional (asked for, not required) or required (a handshake without one that chains to the
clientCertAfter: is refused). What a presented certificate is worth to a protocol — RFC 8705, GET /tls/sign-in, the remote PEP — is on
appliedNext: The TLS policy is applied at the next handshake when a setting changes.
customText: Listeners an administrator defined (#472): HTTPS, bound on every node, each answering only the hosted applications mapped to it — a path of any other is a 404 there. Its TLS settings follow the service's unless its definition's tls says otherwise.
customNone: None: every application is on the main port.
inForceNote: Each value is this listener's own where its row below sets one, and the service-wide default otherwise (inherit, an empty box, or -1 for a number).
applicationsText: Where each hosted application is: the listeners that answer it, and the one its URLs — its issuer, metadata, redirects and mailed links — are built on.
defaultsNote: What every TLS listener inherits unless its own tab or definition says otherwise.
customTabNote: Set in the listener's definition, on the Custom listeners tab.
